# Fluxio — Complete LLM Reference (`llms-full.txt`)

    """Proxy returned by `fig[row, col]` for cell placement and per-cell `.style(...)`."""
    def __init__(self, figure: Figure, row: int, col: int) -> None:
        """Initialize self.  See help(type(self)) for accurate signature."""

class Figure:
    """Global Fluxio visualization container supporting grids, custom styles, terminal print, and exports."""
    def __init__(self, rows: int = 1, cols: int = 1, *, title: str = '', subtitle: str = '', theme: str = 'dark', style: dict[str, Any] | None = None, size: tuple[int, int] = (900, 520), fps: int = 60, toolbar: bool | dict[str, bool] = True) -> None:
        """Initialize self.  See help(type(self)) for accurate signature."""
        ...
    def __getitem__(self, key: tuple[int, int] | int) -> SubplotSlot: ...
    def __setitem__(self, key: tuple[int, int] | int, visual: Visual) -> None: ...
    @property
    def resolved_theme(self) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
    @property
    def is_dynamic(self) -> bool: ...
    def add(self, visual: Visual, *, row: int | None = None, col: int | None = None, row_span: int | None = None, col_span: int | None = None) -> Visual:
        """Attach any `Visual` subclass instance to the Figure grid."""
        ...
    def number(self, value: NumberSource, *, label: str = '', unit: str = '', prefix: str = '', precision: int | None = None, color: str | None = None, description: str = '', row: int | None = None, col: int | None = None, row_span: int = 1, col_span: int = 1) -> Number:
        """Add a static or dynamic `Number` indicator widget to the Figure grid."""
        ...
    def plot(self, x_or_y: Any, y: Any = None, *, label: str = '', color: str | None = None, linewidth: float = 2.4, linestyle: str = 'solid', marker: str | None = None, fill: bool | None = None, fill_alpha: float = 0.12, max_points: int = 120, card_title: str = '', xlabel: str = '', ylabel: str = '', xlim: Sequence[float | None] | None = None, ylim: Sequence[float | None] | None = None, xmin: float | None = None, xmax: float | None = None, xstep: float | None = None, ymin: float | None = None, ymax: float | None = None, ystep: float | None = None, grid: bool = True, legend: bool | str = True, description: str = '', row: int | None = None, col: int | None = None, row_span: int = 1, col_span: int = 1) -> Plot:
        """Add or superpose a 2D line series (`Plot`) on the target grid cell."""
        ...
    def evaluate_frame(self, t: float, *, step_index: int | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: ...
    def to_spec(self, *, t: float = 0.0, step_index: int | None = 0, bake_duration: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
    def to_text(self, *, ansi: bool = True, width: int | None = None, t: float = 0.0, step_index: int | None = 0) -> str: ...
    def reset_print(self) -> Figure: ...
    def print(self, *, duration: float | None = None, fps: int | None = None, controls: bool = True, ansi: bool = True, width: int | None = None) -> None: ...
    def show(self, *, backend: str = 'auto', block: bool = True, host: str = '127.0.0.1', port: int = 0, close_after: float | None = None) -> str: ...
    def save(self, path: str | Path, *, duration: float = 3.0, fps: int | None = None, scale: float = 2.0) -> Path: ...

def show(fig: Figure | Visual, *, backend: str = 'auto', block: bool = True, host: str = '127.0.0.1', port: int = 0, close_after: float | None = None) -> str:
    """Open an interactive Fluxio window (like `matplotlib.pyplot.show()`)."""
    ...
def save(fig: Figure | Visual, path: str | Path, *, duration: float = 3.0, fps: int | None = None, scale: float = 2.0) -> Path:
    """Convenience function calling `fig.save(...)`."""
    ...
def print(fig: Figure | Visual, *, duration: float | None = None, fps: int | None = None, controls: bool = True, ansi: bool = True, width: int | None = None) -> None:
    """Convenience wrapper calling `fig.print(...)` for live in-place terminal/Jupyter display."""
    ...
def llm_context(mode: str = 'compact', *, chart: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Return AI-optimized Fluxio documentation at runtime (`'compact'`, `'full'`, `'stub'`, or `chart='...'`)."""
    ...

## Quickstart in 10 Lines

```python
import math
import fluxio as fx

fig = fx.Figure(rows=1, cols=2, title="Live Telemetry Overview", size=(960, 420), fps=24)
fig.style(background=fx.Gradient(["#090d16", "#1e1b4b"], angle=135), radius=20)

fig[0, 0].style(variant="reverse", accent="#059669", accent_side="left").number(
    42.5, unit="°C", precision=1, label="SoC Temperature"
)
xs = [i * 0.2 for i in range(35)]
fig[0, 1].style(accent="#38bdf8", accent_side="right").plot(
    xs, [math.sin(x) * 30 + 50 for x in xs], label="Signal", xlabel="t (s)"
)

print(fig)                # ANSI TrueColor + Unicode Braille in terminal!
fx.show(fig)              # Interactive desktop window (zoom/pan, pause, PNG capture)
fig.save("overview.png")  # High-DPI export in milliseconds
```

---

<!-- source: docs/tutorial.md -->

# Step-by-Step Tutorial

This tutorial walks you from the **absolute minimal 2-line Fluxio script** up to multi-panel dashboards, custom corporate themes, real-time animated `.gif` / WebSocket streams, and ANSI terminal rendering.

---

## 1. The Minimal Example (2 Lines)

Every Fluxio visualization inherits from `fx.Visual`, meaning **you do not even need to create a `Figure` container** when displaying a single chart or KPI:

=== "Minimal `Plot`"

    ```python
    import fluxio as fx

    fx.Plot([12, 28, 19, 37, 31, 46]).show()
    ```

        !!! info "Specificity: Single-Argument `y`"
        When you pass only one sequence (`[12, 28, ...]`), Fluxio automatically generates `x = [0, 1, 2, ...]` and computes human-readable axis ticks (*nice numbers*) with 6% vertical breathing room.

=== "Minimal `Number`"

    ```python
    import fluxio as fx

    fx.Number(42.5, unit="°C", label="Core Temp").show()
    ```

    === "Terminal (`print`)"

    Replace `.show()` with Python's built-in `print(...)` on **the exact same object** — no extra library (`plotext`) required:

    ```python
    import fluxio as fx

    p = fx.Plot([12, 28, 19, 37, 31, 46], label="Requests")
    print(p)
    ```

    ---

## 2. Multi-Cell Grids & Superposition (`fx.Figure`)

When combining multiple visualizations in one window or slide, create a `Figure(rows, cols)` grid.

### Key Specificities of `Figure` Grids

1. **Two Equivalent Placement Syntaxes**:
   - **Builder methods**: `fig[0, 0].number(...)` or `fig.number(..., row=0, col=0)` (auto-places into the next free slot if `row`/`col` are omitted).
   - **Object assignment**: `fig[0, 0] = fx.Number(...)`.
2. **Row & Column Spans**: Pass `col_span=2` or `row_span=2` to make a header KPI or wide chart span multiple cells.
3. **Automatic Curve Superposition on `Plot`**: Calling `fig[r, c].plot(...)` multiple times on **the same `(row, col)` slot** superposes additional curves onto the same axes (with automatic palette cycling and inline legend) rather than overwriting the cell!

```python
import math
import fluxio as fx

fig = fx.Figure(rows=1, cols=2, title="Thermal Experiment", size=(920, 400))

# Left cell (0, 0): KPI card
fig[0, 0].number(250.0, unit="°C", precision=1, label="Target Asymptote")

# Right cell (0, 1): two superposed curves on the same Plot!
xs = [i * 0.25 for i in range(25)]
fig[0, 1].plot(xs, [800 * math.exp(-0.3 * x) + 250 for x in xs], label="Theory", xlabel="t (s)")
fig[0, 1].plot(
    xs,
    [800 * math.exp(-0.3 * x) + 250 + 35 * math.sin(x * 2) for x in xs],
    label="Sensor",
    linestyle="dashed",
    marker="circle",
)

fx.show(fig)
```

---

## 3. Cascading Aesthetics, Variants & Crescents (`.style()`)

Fluxio separates **data** from **aesthetics** through a chainable `.style(...)` method that cascades from the global `Figure` down to individual cells:

```python
fig = fx.Figure(rows=1, cols=2, title="Corporate KPIs", theme="presentation")

# 1. Global defaults for the entire figure
fig.style(
    background=fx.Gradient(["#090d16", "#1e1b4b"], angle=135),
    accent="#38bdf8",
    accent_side="left",   # Tapered crescent on the left (reading order)
    radius=22,
    hover_ms=220,         # Smooth 220ms hover transition (zero popping!)
)

# Cell (0, 0) inherits global left cyan crescent & translucent light veil
fig[0, 0].number(99.95, unit="%", precision=2, label="Availability")

# 2. Local override on cell (0, 1): solid `reverse` fill + right emerald crescent
fig[0, 1].style(
    variant="reverse",
    accent="#059669",
    accent_side="right",
).number(14.2, unit="ms", precision=1, label="Median Latency")
```

### Specificities Worth Knowing

- **Adaptive Translucent Veil**: In `variant="classic"`, Fluxio computes the WCAG luminance of your background (`#hex`, `fx.Gradient`, or `fx.BackgroundImage`) and automatically picks a subtle **light glass veil (~10% `#ffffff`)** on dark backgrounds or a **dark glass veil (~8% `#0f172a`)** on light backgrounds.
- **PowerPoint Transparency**: Set `fig.style(transparent=True)` before `fig.save("slide.png")` or `fig.save("slide.svg")` to export an alpha-transparent graphic whose card contrast is still calibrated for your target slide color.
- **Graphical TUI Mode (`variant="text"`)**: Switches the Canvas/PNG/SVG renderer to a `btop`-inspired console look (`┤ Label ├` headers, monospace font, and segmented 6-row block-matrix digits):

---

## 4. Real-Time Dynamics & Animated `.gif` / `.mp4` Exports

Any Fluxio chart accepts **dynamic Python sources** without timers, callbacks, or boilerplate threads:

1. **Time Function `Callable[[float], ...]`**: Receives elapsed time `t` in seconds.
   - On `Plot`, returning a **single float** `f(t) -> y` (or `(x, y)` point) automatically activates **Grafana-style rolling window mode** (`max_points=120`).
   - Returning a **pair of sequences** `f(t) -> (xs, ys)` activates **animated waveform mode** (re-draws the entire curve at instant `t`).
2. **Python Generator (`yield`)**: Yields values step-by-step on each frame tick.

```python
import math
import fluxio as fx

fig = fx.Figure(
    rows=1,
    cols=2,
    title="Live Sensor & Travelling Wave",
    size=(880, 380),
    fps=20,
)
fig.style(background=fx.Gradient(["#090d16", "#0f172a", "#1e1b4b"], angle=135), radius=20)

# Left: dynamic KPI oscillating smoothly
fig[0, 0].style(variant="reverse", accent="#059669", accent_side="left").number(
    lambda t: 850.0 + 95.0 * math.sin(2.0 * math.pi * t / 2.0),
    unit="°C",
    precision=1,
    label="Magma Chamber",
)

# Right: animated travelling wave
xs = [i * 0.18 for i in range(36)]
fig[0, 1].style(accent="#38bdf8", accent_side="right").plot(
    lambda t: (
        xs,
        [math.sin(x - 2.0 * math.pi * t / 2.0) * math.cos(x * 0.3) for x in xs],
    ),
    label="Seismic Wave",
    xlabel="Distance (km)",
    ylim=(-1.15, 1.15),
)

# Export directly to an animated GIF, MP4 video, or offline interactive HTML!
fig.save("live_demo.gif", duration=2.0, fps=16)
fig.save("live_demo.mp4", duration=2.0, fps=24)
fig.save("live_demo.html", duration=2.0, fps=24)
```

---

## 5. Live Terminal Rendering (`print(fig)` vs `fig.print()`)

Even dynamic animations work directly inside an SSH session, Raspberry Pi console, or Jupyter Notebook `stdout`:

- **Manual Loop Control (`print(fig)`)**: Calling Python's standard `print(fig)` repeatedly tracks how many lines were printed and uses ANSI cursor-up (`\x1b[<N>A`) in TTY terminals (or `clear_output(wait=True)` in Jupyter) to **update in-place without scrolling**:
  ```python
  import time

  for _ in range(40):
      print(fig)        # Updates in-place on frame 2..40!
      time.sleep(0.05)
  ```
- **Automatic Live Loop (`fig.print()` / `fx.print(fig)`)**: Runs the frame loop for you with live non-blocking keyboard controls (**`Space`** = Pause/Play, **`R`** = Reset, **`Q` / `Ctrl+C`** = Quit):
  ```python
  fig.print()                 # Runs interactively until Q or Ctrl+C
  fig.print(duration=5.0)     # Runs for 5 seconds then exits cleanly
  ```

---

<!-- source: docs/styling.md -->

# Styling & Themes

Fluxio uses a CSS-like **style cascade**:

1. **Preset Theme** (`theme="dark" | "light" | "presentation"`)
2. **Global Figure Style** (`fig.style(...)` — chainable, sets figure background & default card aesthetics)
3. **Per-Cell Style** (`fig[row, col].style(...)` or `cell.style(...)` — overrides only that specific cell)

## Style Variants (`variant`)

Every figure or individual cell supports three visual variants via `.style(variant=...)`:

| Variant | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `"classic"` *(default)* | Adaptive translucent glass veil (~10% light veil on dark backgrounds, ~8% dark veil on light backgrounds) with a tapered rounded crescent on `accent_side`. |
| `"reverse"` | Solid `accent` background fill with auto-contrasted ink (`#ffffff` or `#090d16`) at `text_opacity` (default `0.90` for value, `~0.68` for label/unit). Ideal to highlight a critical KPI card. |
| `"text"` | Modern TUI / console aesthetic (`btop`-style `┤ Label ├` frame, monospace font, and segmented 6-row block-matrix digits) across windows, Jupyter, and PNG/SVG exports. |

## Custom Backgrounds (`background`)

`fig.style(background=...)` accepts:

- **Hex color string**: `"#0b1120"` or `"transparent"` (or `fig.style(transparent=True)` for alpha-transparent PowerPoint exports).
- **Linear or Radial Gradient**:
  ```python
  fig.style(
      background=fx.Gradient(["#090d16", "#1e1b4b", "#0f172a"], angle=135, kind="linear")
  )
  ```
- **Self-contained Image** (auto-encoded to Base64 for offline `.html` & Jupyter):
  ```python
  fig.style(
      background=fx.BackgroundImage("corporate_slide.png", fit="cover", opacity=1.0)
  )
  ```

Fluxio automatically measures the perceived WCAG luminance of solid colors, gradients, and images to pick a harmonious light or dark translucent veil and readable text colors unless explicitly overridden.

## Tapered Crescent Borders & Smooth Hover

- `accent_side`: `"left"` | `"right"` | `"top"` | `"bottom"` | `"none"` (default `"top"`). Renders a CSS-like tapered rounded crescent (`accent_width`, default `7.0`) that merges seamlessly into the thin card border (`border_width`, `border_opacity`).
- `hover_ms`: Smooth `smoothstep` transition duration in milliseconds (default `200` ms) when hovering cards in interactive views — eliminating abrupt visual popping while dropping back to 0% CPU once settled.

---

<!-- source: docs/developer.md -->

# Architecture & 3-Level OOP Hierarchy

This section covers the non-visual engineering backbone of Fluxio: how containers, class inheritance, real-time streaming, and multi-target renderers fit together.

## 1. Hybrid Container + Standalone Objects

Every visualization in Fluxio can be instantiated and rendered **in two equivalent ways**:

1. **Standalone Object** — Every chart inherits from `fx.Visual`, giving it built-in `.style(...)`, `.show()`, `.save(...)`, `.print()`, `print(v)`, and Jupyter `_repr_html_()`:
   ```python
   import fluxio as fx

   p = fx.Plot([10, 25, 18, 32], label="Throughput", title="API Traffic")
   p.style(accent="#34d399", accent_side="left")
   p.save("traffic.png")
   ```
2. **Multi-Cell `Figure` Grid** — Compose heterogeneous charts side-by-side using Matplotlib-style `(row, col)` indexing or builder methods:
   ```python
   fig = fx.Figure(rows=1, cols=2, title="System Dashboard")
   fig[0, 0] = fx.Number(42.5, unit="°C", label="SoC Temp")
   fig[0, 1].plot([10, 25, 18, 32], label="Throughput")
   fx.show(fig)
   ```

---

## 2. Strict 3-Level Inheritance Tree

To keep the codebase modular across 50+ chart types without deep inheritance chains, Fluxio enforces **at most 3 class levels** (`1 concrete chart = 1 dedicated module`):

```text
Visual (Level 1 — style, dynamic lifecycle, standalone show/save/print/Jupyter)
├── Indicator (Level 2 — numeric formatting, units, prefixes)
│   └── Number (Level 3 — src/fluxio/charts/number.py)
├── Axis2D (Level 2 — X/Y bounds, nice ticks, gridlines, labels, Braille canvas)
│   └── Plot (Level 3 — src/fluxio/charts/plot.py)
├── Field2D (Level 2 — 2D matrices, meshes, colormaps, colorbars)
├── Polar2D (Level 2 — radial & angular coordinates)
├── Space3D (Level 2 — 3D camera elevation/azimuth & projection)
└── Scene (Level 2 — node graphs, flame graphs, interactive explainers, simulations)
```

---

## 3. Declarative Scene Protocol & 3 Synchronized Renderers

Python never embeds brittle HTML/JS strings directly per chart. Instead, `Figure.to_spec()` emits a pure **JSON Scene Specification** consumed by three lightweight engines:

| Engine | Implementation | Target Environments |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Canvas 2D Viewer** | Zero-dependency TypeScript (`web/src/`, ~38 KB minified) | `fx.show()` (`pywebview` / `--app` browser), Jupyter inline cells, standalone `.html`, Flutter/Web chatbots |
| **Headless 2D & Vector** | Pure Python (`Pillow` 2x supersampled + `SVG` + `ffmpeg` pipe) | `.png`, `.svg`, `.gif`, `.mp4`, `.webm` (runs in ms on Raspberry Pi with zero Chromium!) |
| **Terminal TUI** | Pure Python ANSI 24-bit TrueColor + Unicode Block & Braille (`2x4` subpixels) | `print(fig)`, `fig.print()` live loop, `.txt`, `.ans` |

---

## 4. Real-Time Streaming Protocol (WebSocket)

When `fx.show(fig)` opens a figure containing dynamic `Callable[[float], ...]` or Python generator (`yield`) sources, `FluxioLiveServer` runs an `asyncio` HTTP + WebSocket loop on `127.0.0.1`:

- **`snapshot`**: Sent on initial connection with the full `FigureSpec`.
- **`tick`**: Streams incremental `{ id, value, formatted }` or `{ id, series_data }` deltas at `fig.fps`.
- **`control`**: Bidirectional toolbar commands (`play`, `pause`, `reset`) sent from the viewer back to Python.

---

<!-- source: docs/outputs.md -->

# Outputs & Exports

A single `fx.Figure` instance supports four output targets without rewriting your code.

## 1. Interactive Desktop Window (`fx.show`)

```python
fx.show(fig)                      # Auto: native pywebview (or GPU --app window on Linux Wayland+NVIDIA)
fx.show(fig, backend="browser")   # Force frameless GPU --app browser window
fx.show(fig, backend="pywebview") # Force pywebview OS WebView
fx.show(fig, backend="terminal")  # Force live in-place terminal mode
```

Interactive toolbar controls (Material SVG icons):

- **Play / Pause & Replay** (for dynamic callable/generator cells, synchronized over local WebSocket)
- **Zoom In / Out / Reset (`100%`)** (buttons, mouse wheel anchored at cursor, double-click reset, touch/mouse drag pan)
- **Capture Screenshot** (instant high-DPI PNG export)
- **Fullscreen**

## 2. Jupyter Notebook Persistence

Place `fig` on the last line of a notebook cell. Fluxio embeds a self-contained, sandboxed HTML viewer (~30 KB, zero CDN links) via `_repr_html_()`:

- Interactive outputs **persist across subsequent cell executions** and remain saved inside the `.ipynb` file offline.
- Mutating `fig` in a later cell (e.g. `fig[0, 1].number(...)`) and evaluating `fig` renders the updated grid cleanly.

## 3. Terminal Rendering (`print(fig)` & `fig.print()`)

No need to switch to `plotext` for console or SSH sessions:

- **Single snapshot or manual loop (`print(fig)`)**:
  ```python
  for _ in range(50):
      print(fig)  # Advances time/generators and overwrites previous lines in-place!
      time.sleep(0.1)
  ```
- **Automatic live TUI loop (`fig.print()` / `fx.print(fig)`)**:
  ```python
  fig.print(duration=5.0, fps=20)  # Omit duration to run until Q or Ctrl+C
  ```
  Supports live keyboard shortcuts in TTY terminals: **`Space`** (Pause/Play), **`R`** (Reset), **`Q` / `Ctrl+C`** (Quit). Also updates in-place inside Jupyter cells via `clear_output(wait=True)`.

## 4. Multi-Format File Exports (`fig.save`)

All exports run headlessly in milliseconds without Chromium:

| Extension | Format | Key Options |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `.png` | High-DPI raster image (RGBA, supports `transparent=True`) | `scale=2.0` |
| `.svg` | Crisp infinite-resolution vector graphic (ideal for PowerPoint) | — |
| `.gif` | Animated GIF evaluated over time | `duration=3.0, fps=20, scale=1.0` |
| `.mp4` / `.webm` | Hardware-compatible H.264 / VP9 video (requires `ffmpeg`) | `duration=3.0, fps=30, scale=1.0` |
| `.html` | 100% self-contained interactive offline web page | `duration=3.0, fps=24` |
| `.txt` / `.ans` | Plain UTF-8 Unicode box-art (`.txt`) or ANSI TrueColor (`.ans`) | — |
| `.term.svg` | Pixel-locked ANSI TrueColor Terminal SVG (zero font misalignment for docs & READMEs) | — |

---

<!-- source: docs/charts/number.md -->

# `Number` / `fig.number()` — Numeric KPI & Live Value Card

Displays a single numeric metric (static value, continuous function of time `f(t)`, or Python generator `yield`).

Inherits from **`Indicator` -> `Visual`** (3-level hierarchy): works both **standalone** (`fx.Number(...).show()`) and **inside a multi-cell `Figure`** (`fig.number(...)`, `fig[r, c].number(...)`, or `fig[r, c] = fx.Number(...)`).

---

## Signatures

```python
# 1. Standalone or assignable object
num = fx.Number(
    value: int | float | Callable[[float], int | float] | Iterator[int | float],
    *,
    label: str = "",
    unit: str = "",
    prefix: str = "",
    precision: int | None = None,
    color: str | None = None,
    description: str = "",
    title: str = "",
    subtitle: str = "",
    theme: str = "dark",
    size: tuple[int, int] = (780, 340),
)

# 2. Directly on a Figure or SubplotSlot
fig.number(
    value: int | float | Callable[[float], int | float] | Iterator[int | float],
    *,
    label: str = "",
    unit: str = "",
    prefix: str = "",
    precision: int | None = None,
    color: str | None = None,
    description: str = "",
    row: int | None = None,
    col: int | None = None,
    row_span: int = 1,
    col_span: int = 1,
) -> Number
```

## Parameters & Specificities

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `value` | `int \| float \| Callable \| Iterator` | *required* | Static number, `fn(t_seconds)` callable, or Python generator yielding numbers. |
| `label` | `str` | `""` | Header title displayed at the top-left of the card (`┤ Label ├` in `text` variant). |
| `unit` | `str` | `""` | Unit suffix displayed next to the number (e.g. `"°C"`, `"%"`, `"ms"`). |
| `prefix` | `str` | `""` | Prefix prepended before digits (e.g. `"€"`, `"$"`). |
| `precision` | `int \| None` | `None` | Fixed decimal places (`None` auto-formats integers cleanly and trims trailing zeros up to 3 decimals). |
| `color` | `str \| None` | `None` | Shorthand hex color override for this cell's accent and value. |
| `description` | `str` | `""` | Context subtitle displayed at the bottom of the card (shown automatically when card height ≥ 130 px). |

!!! tip "Auto-Fitting Typography & `reverse` Contrast"
    - **Overflow protection**: If a formatted number + unit is wider than the card, Fluxio automatically scales the font size down proportionally so digits never clip.
    - **`variant="reverse"`**: Fills the card with `accent` and automatically picks `#ffffff` or `#090d16` ink based on WCAG luminance, applying `text_opacity` (default `0.90` on digits, `~0.68` on label/unit) so text blends harmoniously into the card hue.

---

## Examples

=== "1. Minimal"

    ```python
    import fluxio as fx

    fx.Number(42.5, unit="°C", label="Core Temp").show()
    ```

    === "2. Animated `.gif` (Generator & `f(t)`)"

    ```python
    import itertools
    import math
    import fluxio as fx

    fig = fx.Figure(rows=1, cols=2, title="Live KPI Stream", size=(820, 340), fps=16)
    fig.style(background=fx.Gradient(["#090d16", "#1e1b4b"], angle=135), radius=20)

    # Left: continuous function of time t
    fig[0, 0].style(accent="#f97316", accent_side="left").number(
        lambda t: 850.0 + 110.0 * math.sin(2.0 * math.pi * t / 2.0),
        unit="°C",
        precision=1,
        label="Magma Temp",
    )

    # Right: Python generator (`yield`) in `reverse` style
    fig[0, 1].style(variant="reverse", accent="#2563eb", accent_side="right").number(
        (i * 15 for i in itertools.count(1)),
        unit="pkt",
        precision=0,
        label="Network Packets",
    )

    fig.save("number_anim.gif", duration=2.0, fps=16)
    ```

    === "3. Terminal Output (`print`)"

    ```python
    import fluxio as fx

    n = fx.Number(99.95, unit="%", precision=2, label="Availability", description="SLA > 99.9%")
    n.style(accent="#34d399", accent_side="left")
    print(n)      # Or `n.print()` for live in-place updates!
    ```

---

<!-- source: docs/charts/plot.md -->

# `Plot` / `fig.plot()` — 2D Line & Time-Series Chart

Draws one or more 1D/2D continuous or discrete curves on a modern `Axis2D` coordinate system.

Inherits from **`Axis2D` -> `Visual`** (3-level hierarchy): works both **standalone** (`fx.Plot(...).show()`) and **inside a multi-cell `Figure`** (`fig.plot(...)`, `fig[r, c].plot(...)`, or `fig[r, c] = fx.Plot(...)`). Calling `.plot(...)` multiple times on the same `Plot` or `(row, col)` cell **superposes multiple curves** with automatic palette cycling and legend.

---

## Signatures

```python
# 1. Standalone or assignable object
p = fx.Plot(
    x_or_y: Any = None,
    y: Any = None,
    *,
    label: str = "",
    color: str | None = None,
    linewidth: float = 2.4,
    linestyle: str = "solid",        # "solid" | "dashed" | "dotted"
    marker: str | None = None,       # None | "circle" | "dot"
    fill_alpha: float = 0.12,        # Subtle Grafana-style gradient under curve (0.0 to disable)
    max_points: int = 120,           # Rolling window size for streaming scalar generators/callables
    card_title: str = "",
    xlabel: str = "",
    ylabel: str = "",
    xlim: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ylim: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    grid: bool = True,
    legend: bool = True,
    title: str = "",
    subtitle: str = "",
    theme: str = "dark",
    size: tuple[int, int] = (840, 460),
)

# 2. Directly on a Figure or SubplotSlot (superposes if called multiple times on the same cell!)
fig.plot(x_or_y, y=None, *, label="", color=None, linewidth=2.4, linestyle="solid", marker=None, fill_alpha=0.12, xlabel="", ylabel="", row=None, col=None) -> Plot
```

## Parameters & Specificities

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `x_or_y`, `y` | `Sequence \| Callable \| Iterator` | — | Pass `(x, y)` sequences, a single `y` sequence (`x = 0..n-1`), a `fn(t)` callable, or a Python generator (`yield`). |
| `label` | `str` | `""` | Series name displayed in the top-right legend and magnetic hover tooltip. |
| `card_title` | `str` | `""` | Optional header title inside the top-left of the cell card (distinct from `label`, which names the curve). |
| `color` | `str \| None` | `None` | Hex color for this curve (cycles automatically through Fluxio's high-contrast palette if omitted). |
| `linewidth` | `float` | `2.4` | Stroke thickness in pixels. |
| `linestyle` | `str` | `"solid"` | `"solid"`, `"dashed"`, or `"dotted"`. |
| `marker` | `str \| None` | `None` | Optional point marker: `None` (clean line), `"circle"` (ring with dark center), or `"dot"` (filled circle). |
| `fill` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Shorthand toggle for the area glow (`fill=False` sets `fill_alpha=0.0`; `fill=True` enables area fill). |
| `fill_alpha` | `float` | `0.12` | Vertical gradient fill opacity from the curve down to the `0` baseline (`0.0` for plain Matplotlib-like stroke). |
| `max_points` | `int` | `120` | Sliding ring-buffer length when `x_or_y` yields or returns streaming scalar points. |
| `xlabel`, `ylabel` | `str` | `""` | Horizontal and rotated (`-90°`) vertical axis titles. |
| `xmin`, `xmax` | `float \| None` | `None` | Explicit horizontal lower and/or upper bound (supports partial locking, e.g. `xmin=0` with auto `xmax`). |
| `ymin`, `ymax` | `float \| None` | `None` | Explicit vertical lower and/or upper bound (e.g. `ymin=0` pins the floor at `0` while auto-scaling the ceiling). |
| `xstep`, `ystep` | `float \| None` | `None` | Exact gridline & tick spacing along X and Y (e.g. `xmin=0, xmax=10, xstep=2` draws grid columns at `0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10`). |
| `xlim`, `ylim` | `tuple \| None` | `None` | Shorthand `(min, max)` or 3-tuple `(min, max, step)` (e.g. `xlim=(0, 10, 2)`). |
| `legend` | `bool \| str` | `True` | `"top"` / `True` (dedicated wrapped line right under the bold card title), `"bottom"` (below `xlabel`, Grafana-style), or `False` / `"none"`. |

!!! info "Two Automatic Real-Time Modes"
    `Plot` inspects what your `Callable[[float], ...]` or Python generator returns:

    1. **Scalar `y` or `(x, y)` point** → **Rolling Time-Series Mode** (like Grafana): appends each new sample and keeps the latest `max_points` points.
    2. **Sequence `ys` or `(xs, ys)`** → **Animated Waveform Mode**: replaces the entire curve on each frame (ideal for physics waves, FFT spectra, or moving profiles).

---

## Examples

=== "1. Minimal"

    ```python
    import fluxio as fx

    fx.Plot([12, 28, 19, 37, 31, 46]).show()
    ```

    === "2. Multi-Series & Markers"

    ```python
    import math
    import fluxio as fx

    xs = [round(i * 0.2, 2) for i in range(36)]
    p = fx.Plot(
        xs,
        [75.0 * math.exp(-0.22 * x) + 20.0 for x in xs],
        label="Model",
        xlabel="Time (s)",
        ylabel="Temp (°C)",
        title="Plot — Multi-Series & Area Glow",
    )
    p.plot(
        xs,
        [75.0 * math.exp(-0.22 * x) + 20.0 + 9.0 * math.sin(x * 2.4) for x in xs],
        label="Sensor",
        color="#f97316",
        linestyle="dashed",
        marker="circle",
        fill_alpha=0.05,
    )
    p.show()
    ```

    === "3. Animated `.gif` (Wave & Rolling Stream)"

    ```python
    import math
    import fluxio as fx

    xs = [i * 0.16 for i in range(42)]
    p = fx.Plot(
        lambda t: (
            xs,
            [math.sin(x - 2.0 * math.pi * t / 2.0) * math.cos(x * 0.28) for x in xs],
        ),
        label="Wave Mode",
        xlabel="Position (m)",
        ylabel="Displacement",
        ylim=(-1.15, 1.15),
        title="Travelling Wave Packet",
        size=(760, 380),
        fps=16,
    )
    p.plot(
        lambda t: (
            xs,
            [0.55 * math.cos(x * 1.3 + 2.0 * math.pi * t / 2.0) for x in xs],
        ),
        label="Counter-Wave",
        color="#f97316",
        linestyle="dashed",
        fill_alpha=0.04,
    )

    p.save("plot_anim.gif", duration=2.0, fps=16)
    ```

    === "4. Terminal Braille (`print`)"

    ```python
    import math
    import fluxio as fx

    xs = [i * 0.25 for i in range(28)]
    p = fx.Plot(xs, [math.sin(x) for x in xs], label="sin(x)", xlabel="x")
    p.plot(xs, [math.cos(x) for x in xs], label="cos(x)", linestyle="dashed", color="#f97316")
    print(p)    # High-resolution 2x4 Unicode Braille + ANSI TrueColor!
    ```

---

<!-- source: docs/ai-integration.md -->

# AI & LLM Integration

Fluxio is designed from the ground up so an **LLM inside a chatbot** (even small local quantized models) can generate rich, interactive visualizations in a few lines of Python with zero hallucinations.

## Built-in Runtime Context (`fx.llm_context`)

When embedding Python inside your chatbot application (e.g. Flutter + Python backend), inject Fluxio's prompt reference directly at runtime without network calls:

```python
import fluxio as fx

# 1. Ultra-lightweight .pyi type signatures only (~450 tokens)
stub_prompt = fx.llm_context("stub")

# 2. Compact LLM guide + rules + API signatures (~750 tokens, recommended default)
system_addon = fx.llm_context("compact")

# 3. Specific chart documentation page on demand (for tool-use / RAG)
number_doc = fx.llm_context(chart="number")

# 4. Complete documentation bundle (llms-full.txt)
full_doc = fx.llm_context("full")
```

## Static Files for AI Agents & RAG

At the root of the repository (and served by MkDocs), Fluxio maintains auto-synchronized files generated via `uv run python -m fluxio.ai_docs`:

- **[`llms.txt`](llms.txt)**: Concise index, golden rules for LLM code generation, and condensed `.pyi` signatures.
- **[`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt)**: Full concatenation of all documentation pages and examples in clean Markdown.
- **[`fluxio.pyi`](fluxio.pyi)**: Condensed PEP 484 type stub covering 100% of the public API.
